title: HGCD size-reduction bound giving O(M(n) log n) complexity

problemStatement.plain: AVAILABLE: Formalize half-GCD step size-reduction bound establishing recursive HGCD O(M(n) log n).

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE: master-theorem bound T(n) ≤ (⌊log₂ n⌋+1)·M(n) = O(M(n)·log n) from halving recurrence, verified 0-axiom (PR #34369)
builtItems: cost_le: T(n) ≤ (Nat.log 2 n + 1)*M(n) from T(n) ≤ 2T(⌊n/2⌋)+M(n) + halving-regularity, strong induction (BinaryGcdOQ03OQ02Incomplete01OQ01.lean:87)
depth_eq_size: ⌊log₂ n⌋+1 = Nat.size n (recursion depth = bit-length)
cost_le_size (bit-length form) and cost_le_linear (M=id ⇒ O(n log n))
insights: O(M(n)·log n) is a master-theorem instance independent of the gcd/matrix algebra; only needs halving + O(M(n)) merge
Key engine: Nat.log_of_one_lt_of_le gives log₂ n = log₂⌊n/2⌋+1 (floor), so depth decreases by 1 per level; ceiling variant differs by ±1 rounding
Superlinearity 2M(⌊n/2⌋)≤M(n) is exactly what telescopes the level sums to depth·M(n)
nextSteps: Optional: ceiling-recurrence variant with ratio hypothesis M(a)b≤M(b)a; or connect to parent HGCD via a size(⌈n/2⌉) reduction lemma
